newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Old Mutual doubles fund's foreign holdings.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Old Mutual doubles fund's foreign holdings.

text.p: Old Mutual, South African financial services giant, has doubled the foreign holdings of its flagship Investors Fund to almost 400 million rand during February, senior portfolio manager Jeremy Bolton said Wednesday.
He said the foreign portfolio represented 6.7 percent of the 5.7 billion rand fund and could be moved up towards the government's exchange control limit of 10 percent.
"It represents a renewed interest in South Africa from abroad. Suddenly we are back on the radar screen," he told Reuters.

Bolton said Old Mutual had signed confidentiality agreements preventing disclosure of the identity of its partners in the central Reserve Bank-approved asset swaps, currently the only mechanism for foreign investment by South African resident companies.

Bolton said South African investors were forbidden to offer shares at a discount but acknoweledged that most asset swaps involved a so-called "arrangement fee of one to two percent and these days usually closer to two".
Bolton said 39 percent of the fund's foreign holdings were in the United States, 20 percent in Japan, 11 percent in Britain and 7.8 percent in South-East Asia and Canada.
